trackedGaps.summary: A road segment shorter than NODE_SNAP (18 wu) cannot be built at all: the far endpoint snaps back onto the existing node, so addRoad silently creates nothing and returns empty nodeIds/edgeIds.
trackedGaps.reproducer: net.addRoad([[0,0],[10,0]]) then net.addRoad([[10,0],[20,0]]) -> second call returns {nodeIds:[], edgeIds:[]} and the graph still has 1 edge.
trackedGaps.impact: Silent no-op rather than an explained rejection. Blocks short connector and slip-lane segments, which S04.3 needs.
trackedGaps.actionWhenFixed: Flip the assertion in test/construction.test.js that currently accepts "either builds or explains itself" to require that a short connector between two distinct existing nodes actually builds.
trackedGaps.partialFixByS01_5: S01.5 made this EXPLICIT rather than silent: addRoad now returns reason "the road is shorter than the snapping distance (18 wu), so its ends would land on the same node". This closes the silent-no-op half.
trackedGaps.remaining: Short segments still cannot be BUILT, which S04.3 needs for slip lanes and auxiliary segments. That needs direction-aware snapping or an explicit override, not just a better message.

THE SOAK REGRESSION IS THE IMPORTANT FINDING. The layout change broke the soak fixture, not the game: soak.js clicked hardcoded screen pixels, the dock grew from about 48px to 124px, and the factory click landed on a dock button. The factory was never placed, so houses had no work destination and trips halved from 11 to 6 - and the soak STILL PASSED, because it asserted the house and shop batches but never the factory. The fixture is now in world units converted via worldToScreen, asserts the factory batch, and calls elementFromPoint before every click to refuse a covered point. This is the exact failure mode TESTING.md warns about: browser drawing should use camera transforms derived from fixture world points, computed after a layout change, rather than tweaking arbitrary click constants until green.

The controller throws on an unknown state field. A misspelled key would otherwise become silent state that nothing renders - the same class of bug as a second copy of the active tool, only harder to see. test/browser/ui.js asserts the throw.

The active tool is stored once. main.js reads ui.activeTool, the dock subscribes for its pressed and visible state, and boot() publishes it to the canvas class from a single subscription. No component keeps its own copy.

Panels are exclusive: ui.set({openPanel}) is the only way to open the menu or the inspector, so showPanel closes the other rather than leaving two booleans to drift. The menu also closes on outside pointerdown and on Escape, and Escape now cancels the innermost thing (dialog, then panel, then road draft, then inspector) instead of help-then-tool.

New map confirms only when dirty, which is set by building a road, roundabout, traffic light or building, and by bulldozing. Save clears it. Autosave deliberately does NOT: the autosave slot is a safety net, not the player's save, so discarding the city still deserves a prompt.

closedGaps.summary: eightCrossingsWorld resolves 6 junctions instead of the expected 8.
closedGaps.fix: resolveCrossings walks a frontier of edges and keeps splitting until no crossing remains, bounded by max(200, edges*8). Each split replaces one edge with two so the edge count strictly increases; budget exhaustion returns false so the caller rolls the whole transaction back.
closedGaps.verification: eightCrossingsWorld reports 8 junctions at x=0..700; a 20-crossing fixture reports 20. Mutation (budget 12) fails 2 tests.

closedGaps.summary: addRoad with more than two control points produces malformed topology. A four-corner closed loop drawn as ONE call yields 6 edges and 5 nodes (expected 4 edges) including a degree-6 hub and TWO separate nodes at identical coordinates, so the loop never closes.
closedGaps.fix: addRoad samples the whole control path once and segments it at real junctions and endpoints only, slicing the sampled polyline instead of re-splicing repeated control prefixes. A path returning to its own start reuses the first station node.
closedGaps.verification: Soak loop is now 4 edges / 4 nodes all degree 2 (was 6 edges, degree-6 hub, duplicate coincident nodes). One-call loop matches four-call topology. Mutation fails 2 tests.

closedGaps.summary: Vehicles deadlocked in a small city: 3 of 7 stopped, 131s max wait, congestion climbing to 43% in the four-building soak fixture.
closedGaps.fix: A degree-2 node is a BEND, not an intersection. _mustYield exempts degree-2 nodes from the cross-traffic yield logic (occupied-zone check and yield-to-the-right scan), which at a corner fired in both directions because the two edges have different axes so _crosses() is always true. The anti-gridlock check is deliberately NOT exempted, since it prevents rear-ending a stopped car across an edge boundary where per-lane car following cannot see it.
closedGaps.verification: Diagnostic exits 0: 0 of 3 stopped, 0.1s max wait, 1.4% congestion, 11 trips (was 8). Soak shows 11 trips and 1% congestion with XP 35.1% (was 8 trips, 43%, 25.5%). Unit 189/189, browser 10/10. Mutation-verified: reverting the exemption fails 1 test, removing the anti-gridlock check fails 1 test.

closedGaps.summary: Economy.toJSON() omits _pendingReturns, cancelledReturns and cancellationReasons, so saving during the dwell loses the queued return trip. No crash or corruption; the trip is simply lost.
closedGaps.fix: The v2 snapshot stores pendingReturns, cancelledReturns, cancellationReasons, RNG states, the simulation clock, stats, the car ID counter, camera and settings. hydrateWorld rebuilds the queue and rebinds callbacks instead of serializing closures.
